item.text: {"reviews":[{"benchmark":"arc","instrument_review":"MESA supports interpreting ARC-AGI-2 scores as performance on unfamiliar grid problems under specified evaluation conditions. The tasks, scoring software and verified-testing rules are documented, and marking tests occurred. Partial-input scoring must be distinguished from fully solving a problem. Repeated-run uncertainty, sensitivity to changed conditions and transfer beyond grid problems remain unresolved. No aggregate quality score is calculated.","supported_claims":["The benchmark evaluates inference of grid transformations from examples.","Official scoring averages input-level correctness within problems, then averages problem scores.","Human solving results informed selection of test sets with similar human difficulty.","Public marking tests cover several correct and incorrect output cases."],"documented_problems":["Software can award partial problem credit although the dataset reserves 'fully solved' for every input being correct.","Verified evaluations use one run rather than an average of repeated runs.","Published corrections include erroneous squares and unclear examples.","The change record does not recalculate every affected AI score."],"missing_information":["Repeated-run score variation and uncertainty estimates for AI comparisons.","Systematic tests of changes to instructions, presentation and software.","Evidence connecting grid scores to broader abilities or real-world performance.","Complete verification of the reported public evaluation archive."],"reinterpretations":["For AI evaluation, unfamiliar-rule reasoning is operationalized through exact grid outputs.","An AI score reflects the evaluated system, settings, spending limit and two permitted attempts.","Human difficulty matching does not establish equivalent difficulty or score stability for AI systems."],"closing_note":"The distinction between partial problem credit and fully solving a problem needs explicit reporting. Human study findings should not be treated as AI reliability evidence.","mesa_answers":[{"id":1,"choice":"Yes","comment":"The version, public test set and official scoring software are identified."},{"id":2,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Rule inference, evaluated AI systems and comparison uses are described."},{"id":3,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Example grids, new inputs and exact required outputs are described."},{"id":4,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Verified evaluations specify settings, spending limits and permitted attempts; other routes may differ."},{"id":5,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Exact input matching and averaging within and across problems are explained."},{"id":6,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Inferring transformations from examples is explicitly linked to learning new rules."},{"id":7,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Puzzle sources, human difficulty selection and duplicate-rule removal are explained; coverage of broader reasoning is not established."},{"id":8,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Developer review and human solving informed selection, but explicit checking of all reference outputs is unclear; later corrections are documented."},{"id":9,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Grid tasks support part of the reasoning claim, without evidence covering broader intelligence."},{"id":10,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Exact outputs directly assess successful grid completion, but alternative routes to credit remain incompletely assessed."},{"id":11,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"The averaging rule is clear, but evidence supporting its interpretation as a combined ability measure is absent."},{"id":12,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Public software tests cover correct grids, wrong sizes, changed squares and missing outputs; coverage is limited."},{"id":13,"choice":"Partly","comment":"AI scores and human solving results provide context, but the human study pool exceeds the final set and testing routes differ."},{"id":14,"choice":"No","comment":"The verified-testing policy explicitly uses one run; repetition for other reported evaluations is unclear."},{"id":15,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"No systematic study of changed instructions, presentation or software is supplied."},{"id":16,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"No score-variation estimates or ranges are supplied."},{"id":17,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Design and review address program-search shortcuts and repeated rules, without comprehensive investigation."},{"id":18,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Exposure monitoring and provider agreements address hidden-data risks, but public exposure and possible leakage remain unresolved."},{"id":19,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Development training is allowed, evaluation-specific changes are discouraged and repeated feedback-driven improvement is restricted to preserve evaluation separation."},{"id":20,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"No supplied study connects scores to language, social interaction or real-world work."},{"id":21,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Verified settings are recorded, but differing testing routes and limited AI comparability evidence remain."},{"id":22,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Public tasks, software and marking tests support inspection; hidden materials and complete result records are not fully available or verified."},{"id":23,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Public licensing and hidden-data confidentiality, provider-handling and code-review rules are stated."},{"id":24,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Dated corrections and code changes are recorded, but their effects on all affected scores are not established."},{"id":25,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Grid-performance claims have direct support; connections to broader intelligence exceed the supplied validation."}]},{"benchmark":"designqa","instrument_review":"MESA supports using DesignQA to examine performance on its Formula SAE document and drawing tasks under the reported information conditions. Practical materials support task relevance, and some marking and setup tests occurred. Wording-sensitive scoring, unequal information supply and limited task coverage constrain interpretation. Evidence for close rankings, transfer to other documents and broader engineering competence is insufficient. No aggregate quality score is calculated.","supported_claims":["The benchmark contains 1,451 question-and-answer pairs across six engineering task groups.","The tasks use practical rules, vehicle materials and test data.","Some marking checks and tests of changed passages and visual information occurred.","Scores describe systems together with their supplied or retrieved information."],"documented_problems":["Wording and formatting can affect credit, including missing commas and valid rules omitted from reference answers.","Task groups are highly uneven, while the overall score weights them equally.","Systems receive different information supplies.","All described scale-bar drawings comply, allowing an always-yes response to earn decision credit on that portion.","One released answer file has fewer rows than the corresponding published question count.","Historical inputs, settings and software are not fully linked to each reported result."],"missing_information":["A complete study of marking accuracy and consistency.","Identical-condition repeated runs and adequate uncertainty estimates for close comparisons.","Systematic prior-exposure checks and clear training and repeated-submission rules.","Evidence of transfer to other technical documents or engineering projects.","Complete reproduction records, score-impact change documentation and access and reuse rules."],"reinterpretations":["Engineering understanding is operationalized through selected Formula SAE questions and supplied reference answers.","AI performance includes the effects of retrieval and information supply.","Text-similarity credit can reflect wording agreement in addition to engineering understanding."],"closing_note":"Tests using changed passages should be distinguished from identical-condition repetition. Group and overall scores require cautious interpretation because task sizes and marking methods differ.","mesa_answers":[{"id":1,"choice":"Yes","comment":"The original benchmark, question count, task groups and public scoring methods are identified."},{"id":2,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Engineering document abilities, AI comparisons and broader intended interpretations are described."},{"id":3,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Rules, drawings, images and required text or yes/no responses are described."},{"id":4,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Instructions, settings and information routes are described, but historical inputs and settings are not fully linked to every result."},{"id":5,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Marking methods and equal weighting of the six groups are explained."},{"id":6,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Tasks are linked to finding, interpreting and applying engineering requirements in practical work."},{"id":7,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Practical sources support relevance, but one rulebook and uneven task counts limit the selection's justification for broader use."},{"id":8,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Additional reviewers checked manually written questions, with exceptions and narrower checks for some explanations."},{"id":9,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Six groups cover several relevant activities, but one rulebook and a limited task range constrain coverage."},{"id":10,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Correct decisions and relevant answers earn credit, but wording, formatting and incomplete references also affect marks."},{"id":11,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"Equal group weighting is described without evidence validating the combined score or distinct group abilities."},{"id":12,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Small marking-test files and discussion of scoring problems establish some checking, without complete validation."},{"id":13,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Random guessing and other AI systems provide comparisons, but information supplies differ and no engineer baseline is reported."},{"id":14,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"Five passage sets change the conditions and therefore do not establish identical-condition repeated testing."},{"id":15,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Effects of changed passages, dimension labels, scale bars and highlighted images were examined."},{"id":16,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Passage-set variation provides limited information, but uncertainty is insufficient for small differences in the main comparisons."},{"id":17,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Formatting, retrieval and familiarity influences were examined; the always-yes opportunity is inferred rather than shown to have been tested."},{"id":18,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Image novelty and possible exposure are discussed, but systematic overlap checks and protected evaluation data are not established."},{"id":19,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"Clear training and repeated-submission rules were not available in the reviewed sources."},{"id":20,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"No supplied evidence establishes transfer to other standards, documents or real engineering projects."},{"id":21,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Information differences are described and some setup effects are tested, but comparisons do not isolate the AI from its information supply."},{"id":22,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Public materials support inspection, but incomplete historical records and an answer-file discrepancy prevent complete reproduction."},{"id":23,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"A licence file and complete responsible-reuse rules were not found; this does not establish that reuse is prohibited."},{"id":24,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Code history identifies revisions, but no clear record explains their effects on scores."},{"id":25,"choice":"Partly","comment":"The paper acknowledges scope and marking limits, while broader competence claims and close rankings need further support."}]}]}
